title: Josh Jacobs charged with two misdemeanors
dek: The Brown County District Attorney's Office has charged Packers running back Josh Jacobs with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property tied to his May arrest in Wisconsin. Prosecutors declined to pursue a felony strangulation charge and two other misdemeanors.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Jacobs faces formal criminal charges after prosecutors narrowed the original charge slate from five counts, dropping the most serious felony strangulation allegation but advancing two misdemeanors.
bottom_line: Watch for the NFL's investigation under the Personal Conduct Policy to proceed independently of the criminal charges. The league may move on its own timeline; the outcome of criminal proceedings will inform but not determine a suspension decision.
body: The Brown County District Attorney's Office has formally charged Packers running back Josh Jacobs with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property stemming from his May arrest in Wisconsin related to a domestic disturbance.

According to Yahoo NFL, the two misdemeanor charges represent a reduced charge slate from the original arrest. Prosecutors declined to move forward with a felony charge of strangulation and suffocation or two other misdemeanors that were initially filed.

Jacobs has remained available to practice and play for the Packers since the arrest. He could face discipline under the NFL's Personal Conduct Policy as a result of the charges, which is typically invoked in cases involving alleged domestic incidents.

Packers General Manager Brian Gutekunst signaled at a press conference this week that the team has already prepared for a possible suspension during the 2026 season, indicating the organization views a Personal Conduct Policy investigation as a real possibility and has begun contingency planning accordingly.
